newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: Bolivia resumes search for Che Guevara's body.
newsitem.headline: Bolivia resumes search for Che Guevara's body.

text.p: The Bolivian government on Tuesday gave the go-ahead for the search to resume for the remains of legendary revolutionary Ernest "Che" Guevara, executed in the jungle in 1967.

Interior Secretary Jose Luis Harb gave the government's official authorisation in the town of Vallegrande, in the jungle mountains of the southeast, where witnesses say the Argentine-born Cuban revolutionary hero was secretly buried.

Harb said the new search would be carried out by Cuban experts using modern detecting equipment. Argentine and Cuban experts gave up their search one year ago after six months' frustrated excavations, which only turned up the bodies of some of Che's fallen guerrilla comrades.
Guevara, who chose Bolivia to launch his doomed attempt to carry Cuban communism to the Latin American mainland, was captured by Bolivian troops in October 1967 and executed in a village schoolhouse.
His corpse was displayed as a trophy to the world press, then buried at a secret site.
